title: Automated geo-fleet drift detection and graceful DNS switchover runbook
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Create an automated detection + mitigation flow for subtle cross-region fleet drift that causes a rising class of production incidents: long tail KV cache inconsistencies and partial routing to stale proxies. Deliverables: 1) detection engine that surfaces geo-fleet drift (health + traffic divergence + KV miss delta), 2) an operator-safe DNS switchover playbook that performs a phased change of upstream edge records with canarying and rollback windows, 3) an automated remediation job that will optionally rehome affected tenants to healthy pools when thresholds are exceeded. The goal is to reduce manual toil during multi-region degradations, improve MTTR, and avoid broad customer-facing degradations during capacity rehoming.
steps: Detection: roll out a per-region drift metric that combines 1-min KV miss rate delta, 99th p90 request latency delta, and RPC error spike. Alert threshold = 3x historical baseline or sustained > 0.8% KV miss delta over 10 minutes.
Triage: run quick-score script to identify impacted tenant slices and classify severity (P0: >5% tenant errors OR >30% latency increase for high-tier customers).
Containment: if severity = P0, invoke soft-traffic-redirect to local warm-standby pools (weighted shift 10% -> 30% -> 100% over 3 minutes) while validating KV hit rate recovery at each step.

DNS Switchover: update edge A/ALIAS records with TTL bump to 60s during canary, perform parallel health probes from 5 regions, and only promote when 5 consecutive probes succeed. Maintain previous records for fast rollback.
KV Consistency: trigger a background resync job for impacted tenant slices. Job runs with token-limited concurrency and emits per-tenant progress; cancel if latency impact observed > 10%.
Verification: run end-to-end acceptance using synthetic tenants and customer-supplied smoke prompts. Validate 99th latencies, KV hit rate, and model response correctness before closing incident.
Rollback: immediately revert DNS records and traffic weights if probe failures exceed 2 within a 5-minute window or if errors increase post-switchover.
Postmortem: capture timeline, root cause, corrective actions, and a metricized SLA impact summary. Plan RCA and hotfix tasks in next cycle if fix requires runtime changes.
Customer comms: prepare templated messages for affected customers (status updates at T+30m / T+2h / T+24h) and involve CSMs for high-tier accounts.
